scope.upstream: controlled mock, no external model API calls
scope.capacity_semantics: locked mode uses transactional counters; background mode permits transient multi-instance overshoot
scope.latency: client success percentiles are empirical order statistics; rejected, dropped and failed calls are counted separately
scope.overhead: attempt time minus upstream read/forward time; excludes request-summary publication and is not direct-vs-gateway A/B
scope.telemetry: before/after per-process counter deltas; includes resource-sampling/drain boundary work; stage means have different denominators and must not be summed
scope.occupancy: saved HTTP windows, including HTTP tails, sampled about every 200 ms; excludes subsequent drain; failed tests may not have saved all windows; over-limit durations are sampled estimates
scope.sql_statements: capacity-lock operation counters are available; complete SQL statement and commit totals are not collected
scope.limits: shared host and middleware; finite controlled loads do not establish production capacity or SLO

interpretation: All traffic uses a controlled local mock; no direct versus real model A/B was performed.
Driver 1 search rates are conservative observations and can be affected by audit alignment and recovery; fixed-rate studies are separate.
Driver 2 waits for permit recovery and records that wait, preheats refined rates, observes drain up to 120 seconds, and keeps the acceptance limit at 5 seconds.
Background mode is a soft multi-instance capacity limit; publish actual observed peaks and overshoot.
Stage and resource observations include measurement/drain boundary work; complete SQL statement and commit counts are unavailable.
Finite shared-host samples do not establish a production maximum or availability SLO.
